newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Labour, Alliance parties start talks.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Labour, Alliance parties start talks.

text.p: New Zealand Labour and Alliance leaders on Monday began talks on Alliance support for a possible coalition between Labour and the New Zealand First Party.
Alliance leader Jim Anderton told reporters he may need more than one meeting with Labour.
"We will assess the documentation we discuss now, and then we will be able to give Labour an indication whether we need to talk again," he said.
He said any agreement with Labour would need to be taken before a combined meeting of Alliance MPs and the party's executive council, probably on Tuesday.
Labour and NZ First would jointly hold 54 seats in the 120-member parliament, and would need the support of the 13 Alliance MPs on money supply and confidence votes.
Anderton has consistently said he will not give a "blank cheque" promise of support without being briefed and consulted on the policy programme of such a government.
NZ First is also negotiating with the caretaker National Party government, and is expected to announce its decision on Tuesday. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 473-4746
